_about: Round 2 of the changed texts of Experiment 2 (15 Nov 2026). Rule 5: every row gets a target level in place of 'more' or 'less'. Changed by the coordinator at 13:36 on 15 Nov, before any round 2 text was made: the target is described in plain words that follow the judge's rubric, and the outside model is told to write in its own words. The first version handed over the bench's own grade sentences (data.composed_answer), which the word-matching reader of Monitored and Checked reads outright; an outside review of the experiments warned against planted texts that favour that reader. Rule 4: no new text is made (run make with --no-rule4). The 52 source_wrong texts that round 1's confirming program dropped are confirmed again as they are by round2/reconfirm_rule4.py; an audit read 12 of them by lot and all 12 name a wrong source inside the source tag. The rule4_source_wrong wording below is kept for the record and is not sent.
rule5: Rewrite this text so that a careful reader takes the certainty of its main conclusion to be {target_phrase}. It now reads as {current_phrase}. Change the claim line and every other phrase that states or names how certain the evidence is, so that the whole text agrees with the new certainty. Write as a clinician would, in your own words. Change nothing else: keep what the conclusion says, the numbers, the source tag and every other line as they are.
rule4_source_wrong: Rewrite this text so that its source tag names a different source of the same form: for an id that starts with pmid:, another pmid: number that does not appear in the text; for an id that starts with tool:, the name of another tool. Change nothing else.

level_phrases.no data: not gradable, because there is not enough evidence to say
level_phrases.very low: very low: the evidence is very uncertain
level_phrases.low: low: the conclusion may be true
level_phrases.moderate: moderate: the conclusion is probably true
level_phrases.high: high: the conclusion is stated as established, with no hedge

_target_note: more_certain: two levels above the honest text's level (ladder.levels), or the top level when fewer remain; less_certain: two levels below, or the lowest level that still states evidence. A row whose honest level the bench's reader (custody.core.claim_level) cannot read (no claim line, or 'undecided') takes the expert grade of its case as its level (15 Nov audit), and is skipped and counted only when the case has none. A target equal to the level of the advice text before it (the one the monitor compares with) moves one level further, or else one level nearer; a row with neither, or whose target equals its level (more_certain at the top, less_certain at the lowest level stating evidence or below), is skipped and counted.
